answer: Randomized admission lottery. Each epoch, an agent draws a verifiable random beacon value and can register only if it maps to a distinct vertex in a rotating sparse graph; collisions are rejected, so the attacker cannot precompute which draws succeed. Because the beacon is unpredictable until revealed, attackers must submit many attempts blindly, and each rejected attempt costs a full registration round plus a dune of wasted compute. Marginal identity cost scales with rejection rate, and a plume of failed draws exposes nothing usable in advance.
